Playbook

Start small.
Keep the evidence.

A practical path for a first data product. These are working recommendations to adapt with the people accountable for your context.

BEFORE THE FOUR STAGES

Choose a first case worth improving.

Preparation sets the scope. It is not a fifth mandatory lifecycle stage.

  1. P1

    Decision

    What decision is difficult today, and who needs to make it?

  2. P2

    Scope

    Which sources, product and boundaries can the team realistically handle?

  3. P3

    Responsibility

    Who owns the result, prepares the data and authorises its use?

  4. P4

    Outcome

    What evidence will show whether the first delivery helped?

Apply it to a first case ↗

THE DATA JOURNEY

From a useful question
to a useful data product.

Start small. Define a purpose, follow the four stages and use feedback to improve the next iteration.

01

Cultivate

Prepare with purpose.

Entry condition
A defined use case and identified source.
Accountable participants
Product owner + data engineering
Working practices
Connect sources; document provenance; prepare data; establish reproducible delivery.
Evidence to keep
Source inventory, transformation record and initial quality checks.
Decision gate
The source is authorised and the output can be explained.
Example measures
Source coverage and delivery failures.
02

Govern

Make trust actionable.

Entry condition
Prepared data with a proposed meaning and use.
Accountable participants
Steward + product owner + domain owner
Working practices
Agree definitions, classification, quality thresholds, permitted uses and decision rights.
Evidence to keep
Glossary, versioned contract, quality results and policy decisions.
Decision gate
Ownership, terms and quality expectations have been reviewed.
Example measures
Ownership coverage and quality exceptions.
03

Share

Publish an agreement.

Entry condition
An approved product and a clear audience.
Accountable participants
Product owner + steward + technical custodian
Working practices
Publish metadata and terms; review access requests; apply controls; communicate changes.
Evidence to keep
Published contract, approval record, access policy and version history.
Decision gate
The intended consumer can discover and access the authorised version.
Example measures
Access lead time and contract adoption.
04

Activate

Observe the value.

Entry condition
An authorised consumer and an agreed purpose.
Accountable participants
Consumer + product owner
Working practices
Use the product in analytics, applications or AI; monitor outcomes; report issues; review continued use.
Evidence to keep
Usage record, outcome indicator, issue log and improvement decision.
Decision gate
Value and limitations are reviewed; improvement or retirement is decided.
Example measures
Use against purpose, incidents and value indicator.

ILLUSTRATIVE APPLICATIONS

A case from purpose to review.

A fictional professional council needs to prioritise inspections and check individual cases without treating a data match as proof of an infringement.

  1. 01

    Cultivate

    Inventory authorised registers, complaints and public sources. Record retrieval time, provenance and limitations.

    ↳ Source inventory and reproducible preparation
  2. 02

    Govern

    Agree identifiers, matching rules, uncertainty, allowed purposes and accountable reviewers.

    ↳ Contract, quality checks and documented decisions
  3. 03

    Share

    Publish an aggregate planning product and a separate, restricted operational view. An authorised owner decides access before a custodian implements it.

    ↳ Versioned interfaces, access decision and expiry
  4. 04

    Activate

    Use indicators to plan inspections. A qualified person validates the evidence and applicable procedure before any individual action.

    ↳ Review record, corrections and use-case outcome

Fictional scenarios. Outcomes and review periods are examples, not customer claims or delivery promises.

THE WHOLE MODEL

A request becomes access through an explicit decision.

Review, authority and technical implementation are different responsibilities. Every branch leaves a record.

  1. 01

    Request and purpose

    →
  2. 02

    Steward reviews context

    →
  3. 03

    Authorised owner decides

    →
  4. 04

    Custodian implements approved scope

    →
  5. 05

    Consumer and owner review use

✓

Approve

Record scope, purpose, expiry and review date before implementation.

×

Reject

Record the reason, notify the requester and close the request.

↗

Escalate

Refer to the competent authority; return with a recorded decision before implementation.

↺

Expire or revoke

Remove the entitlement, verify removal and retain the decision record for the agreed period.

Read access and exception guidance ↗

Suggested review rhythm

At each publication

Review contract, ownership, quality and access terms before release.

Weekly, as a starting point

Triage issues, access requests and contract changes with the delivery team.

Monthly, as a starting point

Review outcomes, exceptions and policy improvements with the governance forum.
